question: A truck has air brakes. Its governor cut-out pressure is 125 psi. The low air warning must come on before pressure in the service reservoir falls below:
explanation: The rule is 60 psi, or half the governor cut-out pressure if that is lower. Half of 125 psi is 62.5 psi, so 60 psi is the lower number.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the low air pressure warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below 60 psi, or half the governor cut-out pressure if that is lower.
change_note: [VERIFY] 393.51(c) may give 55 psi (or half governor cut-out) for vehicles not under FMVSS 121; 60 psi appears to come from FMVSS 121 (49 CFR 571.121). Confirm before publishing.

question: The governor cut-out pressure is 100 psi. The low air warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below:
explanation: Half of 100 psi is 50 psi. That is lower than 60 psi, so the warning must come on before pressure falls below 50 psi.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the low air pressure warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below 60 psi, or half the governor cut-out pressure if that is lower.
change_note: [VERIFY] 393.51(c) may give 55 psi (or half governor cut-out) for vehicles not under FMVSS 121; 60 psi appears to come from FMVSS 121 (49 CFR 571.121). Confirm before publishing.

question: The warning point is 60 psi or half the governor cut-out pressure. Which one do you use?
explanation: The rule says whichever is less. So you use the lower of the two numbers.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the low air pressure warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below 60 psi, or half the governor cut-out pressure if that is lower.
change_note: [VERIFY] 393.51(c) may give 55 psi (or half governor cut-out) for vehicles not under FMVSS 121; 60 psi appears to come from FMVSS 121 (49 CFR 571.121). Confirm before publishing.

question: The governor cut-out pressure is 140 psi. The low air warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below:
explanation: Half of 140 psi is 70 psi. That is higher than 60 psi, so 60 psi is the lower number and the warning point.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the low air pressure warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below 60 psi, or half the governor cut-out pressure if that is lower.
change_note: [VERIFY] 393.51(c) may give 55 psi (or half governor cut-out) for vehicles not under FMVSS 121; 60 psi appears to come from FMVSS 121 (49 CFR 571.121). Confirm before publishing.

question: The governor cut-out pressure is 90 psi. The low air warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below:
explanation: Half of 90 psi is 45 psi. That is lower than 60 psi, so the warning must come on before pressure falls below 45 psi.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the low air pressure warning must come on before service reservoir pressure falls below 60 psi, or half the governor cut-out pressure if that is lower.
change_note: [VERIFY] 393.51(c) may give 55 psi (or half governor cut-out) for vehicles not under FMVSS 121; 60 psi appears to come from FMVSS 121 (49 CFR 571.121). Confirm before publishing.

question: Federal rules require the brakes on a CMV to be:
options: Used only on the rear wheels
Checked by a mechanic once a year only
Adequate to stop and hold the vehicle or combination
explanation: The brakes must be able to stop the vehicle and hold it still.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: each CMV must have brakes adequate to stop and hold the vehicle or combination of vehicles.

question: As a general rule, a CMV must have brakes acting on:
explanation: There are a few narrow exceptions, such as some older heavy trucks and very light trailers.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: every commercial motor vehicle must be equipped with brakes acting on all wheels, with a short list of exceptions.

question: On a power-braked vehicle, one application valve must operate:
options: All of the service brakes on the vehicle or combination
explanation: A single valve, the foot valve, applies every service brake. A second valve for trailer brakes is also allowed.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: on power-braked vehicles, one application valve must operate all service brakes on the vehicle or combination; a separate trailer brake valve is also allowed.

question: The driver must be able to apply the emergency brake from:
options: Only after unbuckling the seat belt
The normal seating position while wearing any seat belt
explanation: You can reach the control from your seat without taking off your belt.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the driver must be able to apply the emergency brake from the normal seating position while wearing any installed seat belts.

question: Besides service brakes, every CMV must have:
explanation: Each CMV needs a parking brake system as well as service and emergency brake systems.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: each commercial motor vehicle must have a parking brake system in addition to its service brakes.

question: On an air-braked towing unit, the tractor protection valve must work automatically when the unit's air pressure falls to between:
explanation: The valve shuts when air drops into the 20 to 45 psi range. That keeps the truck's air from leaking away through a broken trailer line.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: on air-braked towing units, the tractor protection valve must operate automatically when towing-unit air pressure falls to between 20 and 45 psi.

question: A tractor that tows air-braked trailers needs two ways to apply trailer emergency brakes. One is automatic. The other is:
options: A manual control the seated driver can readily reach
A switch only the shipper can use
explanation: The second way is a manual control the driver can work from the driver's seat. Its emergency position must be clearly marked.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a truck or tractor towing air-braked vehicles needs an automatic means and a manual control that the driver in the driving seat can readily operate.

question: If a trailer breaks away, the towing vehicle's service brakes must still be able to:
options: Work only on the front axle
explanation: A towing vehicle must have a means so its own service brakes can still stop it after a trailer breakaway.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a vehicle that tows a braked trailer must have a means that lets its service brakes stop it if the trailer breaks away.

question: No-bleed-back relay emergency valves protect:
options: The tires from losing air pressure
The towed vehicle's supply reservoir from air flowing back toward the towing vehicle
explanation: These valves keep air from draining out of the trailer's supply tank back toward the truck when truck pressure drops.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: air brake systems on towed vehicles must use no-bleed-back relay emergency valves or equivalent devices.

question: Which device keeps a towing vehicle from losing its air if an air-braked trailer breaks away?
explanation: The tractor protection valve, or a similar device, closes automatically so the truck keeps its air supply.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: air-braked towing units must have a tractor protection valve or similar device that operates automatically when air pressure falls in the set range.

question: Each air brake reservoir must have a condensate drain valve that can be operated:
options: Only when the engine is off
explanation: Automatic drain valves are allowed, but a manual way to drain must remain.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: each reservoir on an air-braked vehicle must have a condensate drain valve that can be operated manually.

question: Check valves in a service reservoir system protect against:
options: Loss of pressure from a leak between the tank and its source
explanation: If a line leaks upstream of the tank, the check valve helps keep the air in the tank.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: each service reservoir system must be protected against loss of pressure from a failure or leak between the reservoir and its source.

question: Brake tubing and hoses must be secured against:
options: Chafing, kinking, or other mechanical damage
explanation: Lines must be held in place so they do not rub through, kink or get damaged.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: brake tubing and hoses must be secured against chafing, kinking or other mechanical damage.

question: Brake tubing and hoses must be installed so they do not touch:
options: The exhaust system or another high-heat source
explanation: Heat can melt or weaken a hose, so lines must stay away from the exhaust.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: brake tubing and hoses must be installed so they do not contact the exhaust system or any other source of high temperature.

question: Coiled nonmetallic brake tubing may be used for connections between:
options: The air compressor and the governor
A towed vehicle and the vehicle towing it
The treadle valve and the brake pedal
A reservoir and a drain valve
explanation: Coiled tubing is meant for the flexible link between a tractor and trailer. It is not for fixed lines on the truck.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: coiled nonmetallic tubing may be used only for connections between towed and towing vehicles or between a trailer frame and an adjustable axle subframe.

question: A CMV with air-activated service brakes must have a pressure gauge and:
explanation: The gauge shows pressure and the warning signal alerts you if pressure gets low.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a CMV with air-activated service brakes, or one towing such a vehicle, must have a pressure gauge and a warning signal.

question: The air brake pressure gauge shows:
options: The air pressure available for braking
explanation: The gauge reads the air pressure that is ready to apply the brakes.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the required gauge must show the air pressure available for braking.

question: CMVs with air brakes made on or after October 20, 1994 must have:
options: Spring brakes on the steering axle only
explanation: Automatic adjusters keep the brakes adjusted without hand work.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: air-braked CMVs made on or after October 20, 1994 must meet the automatic brake adjuster requirements of FMVSS 121.

question: A brake adjustment indicator shows when:
explanation: The indicator warns that the brakes need attention.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the brake adjustment indicator must show when the service brakes are under-adjusted.

question: A CMV with air brakes made on or after October 20, 1994 needs an indicator if it has an outside automatic adjuster and:
explanation: The indicator is required when a vehicle has an outside automatic adjuster and an exposed pushrod.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: an indicator is required on air-braked CMVs made on or after October 20, 1994 that have both an external automatic adjuster and an exposed pushrod.

question: Without retaking the knowledge tests, a commercial learner's permit is valid for no more than:
options: Six months from the day it was first issued
Two years from the day it was first issued
One year from the day it was first issued
Three years from the day it was first issued
explanation: A CLP can last up to one year from its first issue date. You can get a longer period only by retaking the knowledge tests.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a CLP is valid for no more than one year from its first issue date unless the holder retakes the general and endorsement knowledge tests.

question: You may not take the CDL skills test until how long after your CLP is first issued?
explanation: The first 14 days after your CLP is issued must pass before you can take the skills test.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a CLP holder may not take the CDL skills test during the first 14 days after the CLP is first issued.

question: A truck driver with a CLP is on a public road. Where must the CDL holder who supervises sit?
options: In the front seat next to the CLP holder
explanation: In a commercial vehicle the CDL holder sits in the front seat beside the CLP holder and watches over the driving at all times.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: in a commercial vehicle, the supervising CDL holder must sit in the front seat next to the CLP holder and keep the CLP holder under direct observation.

question: A CLP holder may not drive a commercial vehicle that is carrying:
explanation: A CLP is not valid for training in a vehicle that carries hazardous materials.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a CLP holder may not operate a commercial motor vehicle that is transporting hazardous materials.

question: Under the federal rule, the CDL holder who supervises a CLP holder must:
options: Hold a valid CDL with the right group and endorsements
Be an employee of the state
explanation: The supervising driver needs a valid CDL with the right group and any endorsements for that vehicle, and must be allowed to drive it on that trip.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the supervising driver must hold a valid CDL with the proper group and endorsements and be authorized to operate the vehicle on that trip.

question: A driver is convicted of a first major offense, such as leaving the scene of an accident, while driving a CMV with no hazmat. The disqualification is at least:
explanation: A first major offense in a CMV costs you your commercial driving rights for one year.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a first conviction for a major offense while driving a CMV disqualifies the driver for 1 year.

question: A driver has a first major offense while hauling hazardous materials. The disqualification is at least:
explanation: Hauling hazmat raises a first major offense from one year to three years.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a first major-offense conviction while operating a CMV that carries hazardous materials means a 3-year disqualification.

question: A driver is convicted of a second major offense in a separate incident. The federal penalty is:
options: One year longer than the first
explanation: A second major offense in a separate incident means a lifetime disqualification under the federal table.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a second conviction for a major offense from a separate incident carries a lifetime disqualification.

question: Which of these is a major offense under the federal disqualification rules?
options: Driving with a burned-out tail lamp
Leaving the scene of an accident
explanation: Leaving the scene of an accident is on the list of major offenses. The other choices are not.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: leaving the scene of an accident is a major offense that disqualifies a CLP or CDL holder.

question: A driver is convicted of a second serious traffic violation in a CMV within 3 years. The disqualification is:
explanation: A second serious violation in 3 years means 60 days. A third means 120 days.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a second serious traffic violation conviction within 3 years means a 60-day disqualification; a third means 120 days.

question: Speeding is a serious traffic violation when it is at least how many miles per hour over the limit?
explanation: Speeding 15 mph or more over the limit counts as a serious traffic violation.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: speeding 15 mph or more over the posted limit is a serious traffic violation.

question: A driver may not use alcohol within how many hours before going on duty or driving a CMV?
explanation: The federal rule is 4 hours before duty.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver may not use alcohol or be under its influence within 4 hours before going on duty or operating a commercial motor vehicle.

question: A driver breaks the federal on-duty alcohol rule. The driver must be put out of service for:
explanation: A driver who breaks the alcohol rule is placed out of service right away for 24 hours.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver who violates the alcohol rule must be placed out of service immediately for 24 hours.

question: Which is an exception to the ban on having alcohol while on duty in a CMV?
options: A small bottle kept in the cab for later
Alcohol kept in the sleeper berth
Unopened alcohol the driver plans to drink off duty
Alcohol that is listed and carried as part of a shipment
explanation: The only exceptions are alcohol that is part of a manifested shipment and alcohol carried by bus passengers.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: drivers may not possess alcohol on duty, except alcohol that is manifested as part of a shipment or carried by bus passengers.

question: A driver is so tired that driving is unsafe. What does the federal rule say?
options: The driver may not drive the CMV
The driver may drive if stopping every hour
The driver may drive until the next planned stop
The driver may drive if the carrier approves
explanation: A driver may not drive when fatigue or illness makes driving unsafe. The only exception is an emergency, and then only to the nearest safe place.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver may not drive a CMV when fatigue, illness or another cause makes driving unsafe, except in an emergency, and then only to the nearest safe place.

question: Under the federal rule on tired or ill drivers, who may not require or allow an impaired driver to drive?
options: No one; it is the driver's choice
explanation: The rule also covers carriers. A carrier may not make or let a driver drive while too tired or ill.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a motor carrier may not require or permit a driver to operate a CMV while impaired by fatigue, illness or another cause.

question: Your CMV is stopped at a red light with the engine running. May you text?
options: Yes, if the light is long
Yes, if you are in the left lane
explanation: Short stops caused by traffic or signals still count as driving when the engine is running.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: driving includes brief stops caused by traffic or signals with the engine running, so texting is not allowed then.

question: For the texting rule, when is a driver not considered to be driving?
options: After pulling off the road to a spot where the vehicle can safely stay stopped
While stopped in traffic with the engine running
While rolling slowly in a traffic jam
While stopped at a traffic light
explanation: You are not driving once you safely move off the road and the vehicle can stay stopped.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver who moves the vehicle off the road to a place where it can safely remain stationary is not considered to be driving.

question: A driver may use a hand-held phone while driving only to:
explanation: The one exception is an emergency call to police or other emergency services.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver may use a hand-held mobile phone while driving only when needed to reach law enforcement or emergency services.

question: A CMV driver whose seat has a seat belt must:
options: Wear it only when the truck is loaded
Wear it only on trips over 50 miles
explanation: The rule applies whenever you drive. It is not limited to certain roads or loads.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver of a CMV with a seat belt at the driver's seat must be properly restrained by the belt whenever driving.

question: Under the federal texting rule, a motor carrier may not:
options: Give drivers a phone to use
Allow or require its drivers to text while driving
Ask for a report when the driver is parked
Let drivers use a phone after safely pulling off the road
explanation: The rule binds carriers too. A carrier may not make or let a driver text while driving.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: motor carriers may not allow or require their drivers to engage in texting while driving.

question: A property-carrying driver may drive up to how many hours inside the 14-hour window?
explanation: The driving limit is 11 hours. It must all fit inside the 14-hour window.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a property-carrying driver may drive a total of 11 hours within the 14-hour period after coming on duty.

question: After 10 consecutive hours off duty, driving is not allowed after how many consecutive hours from coming on duty?
explanation: The 14-hour window keeps running, even during breaks, until the driver has another 10 hours off duty.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver may not drive after the 14th consecutive hour from coming on duty following 10 consecutive hours off duty.

question: Before a property-carrying driver starts driving, the driver needs how many consecutive hours off duty?
explanation: A driver starts each driving period after 10 consecutive hours off duty.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a driver may not drive without first having 10 consecutive hours off duty.

question: A driver may not drive once how many hours of driving have passed without a break of at least 30 minutes?
explanation: The break can be off duty, sleeper berth or on duty but not driving. It must last at least 30 consecutive minutes.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: driving is not allowed after more than 8 hours of driving time without an interruption of at least 30 consecutive minutes.

question: A driver for a carrier that operates every day of the week may not drive after 70 hours on duty in:
explanation: Carriers that run every day use the 70-hour, 8-day limit. Others use 60 hours in 7 days.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: if the carrier operates every day, a driver may not drive after 70 hours on duty in 8 consecutive days; otherwise the limit is 60 hours in 7 days.

question: A 7-day or 8-day period may end when a driver has an off-duty period of at least:
explanation: A 34-hour off-duty period lets the weekly count start over.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a 7-day or 8-day period may end when the driver has 34 or more consecutive hours off duty.

question: Before driving, a driver must be satisfied that which of these is in good working order?
options: The service brakes, including trailer brake connections
explanation: The list includes the brakes, parking brake, steering, lights and reflectors, tires, horn, wipers, mirrors, coupling devices, wheels and rims, and emergency equipment.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: before driving, the driver must be satisfied that parts such as service brakes, steering, tires, lights and coupling devices are in good working order.

question: When must a driver write a vehicle inspection report?
options: At the end of each day's work on each vehicle driven
explanation: The driver writes the report at the end of the day's work. If no defect was found or reported, no report is required.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the driver must prepare a written report at the completion of each day's work on each vehicle operated, unless no defect was found or reported.

question: How long must the motor carrier keep the inspection report and repair certification?
options: 3 months from the date of the report
explanation: The carrier keeps the report and the record of repairs for three months.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the carrier must keep the report, the repair certification and the driver review certification for three months from the report date.

question: Before driving, what must a driver be satisfied about?
options: That the vehicle is in safe operating condition
That the trip will end before dark
That the fuel tanks are full
explanation: The driver must also review the last inspection report and sign it when the rule requires.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: before driving, a driver must be satisfied that the motor vehicle is in safe operating condition.

question: A CMV must pass a periodic inspection at least once every:
explanation: The periodic inspection is a yearly check of the parts on the federal list.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: each CMV must pass an inspection of the required components at least once during the preceding 12 months.

question: Which can serve as proof of a passed periodic inspection kept on the vehicle?
options: A receipt from a fuel stop
A page from the driver's log
A sticker or decal that shows the date and carrier details
A spoken statement from the driver
explanation: The proof must be on the vehicle. It can be the report or a sticker or decal with the date, carrier details and a pass statement.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: proof of a passed periodic inspection must be on the vehicle, such as the report or a sticker or decal showing the date, carrier details and that it passed.

question: After a truck driver starts a trip, cargo and its securement devices must be inspected within the first:
explanation: The first check comes within 50 miles. After that, re-check on the schedule.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a truck driver must inspect the cargo and its securement devices within the first 50 miles after beginning a trip and make needed adjustments.

question: During a trip, the driver must re-examine cargo when the duty status changes, or after how much driving, whichever comes first?
explanation: Check again after a duty status change, 3 hours of driving or 150 miles, whichever comes first.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the driver must re-examine cargo and securement when changing duty status, or after the vehicle has been driven 3 hours or 150 miles, whichever occurs first.

question: Which driver is excused from the en-route cargo inspection rule?
options: A driver who is running late
A driver of a sealed vehicle who was ordered not to open it
A driver carrying a light load
A driver on an interstate highway
explanation: A sealed vehicle that the driver was ordered not to open is exempt. So is a load that makes inspection impracticable.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the cargo inspection rules do not apply to a driver of a sealed vehicle ordered not to open it, or one loaded so inspection is impracticable.

question: The minimum tread depth for steering axle tires on a truck or tractor is:
explanation: Steering tires need more tread than the others. The depth is measured in a major tread groove.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: tires on the steering axle of a bus, truck or truck tractor must have at least 4/32 inch of tread in a major groove.

question: The minimum tread depth for tires that are not on the steering axle is:
explanation: All tires other than steering axle tires need at least 2/32 inch in a major groove.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: all tires other than those on the steering axle must have at least 2/32 inch of tread in a major tread groove.

question: A tire must not be used on a CMV if:
options: Body ply or belt material shows through the tread or sidewall
It is a different brand than the others
It has been retreaded on a rear axle
It has more than 50,000 miles on it
explanation: Exposed ply or belt material means the tire is unsafe. Brand and retreading on rear axles are not the issue.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a CMV may not run on a tire that has body ply or belt material exposed through the tread or sidewall.

question: A CMV stops on the shoulder for a reason other than a traffic stop. What must the driver do first?
options: Turn on the hazard warning flashers
explanation: Turn on the flashers right away and keep them on until the warning devices are out.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: when a CMV stops on the traveled part of the road or shoulder, the driver must immediately activate the hazard flashers and keep them on until warning devices are placed.

question: Warning devices must be placed as soon as possible and within:
explanation: The rule gives you at most 10 minutes to put out the devices.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: warning devices must be placed as soon as possible and in any event within 10 minutes of stopping.

question: On an undivided road, how far from the stopped CMV is the farthest warning device placed, toward oncoming traffic?
explanation: Place one near the truck, about 10 feet away, one about 100 feet toward oncoming traffic and one about 100 feet behind the truck.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the general rule places one device about 10 feet toward traffic and one about 100 feet away on each side, ahead and behind.

question: On a divided or one-way road, where are the warning devices placed?
options: At 200 feet and 100 feet toward traffic, and within 10 feet of the rear
explanation: On divided or one-way roads, put one at 200 feet and one at 100 feet toward traffic, and one within 10 feet of the rear.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: on a divided or one-way road, place one device 200 feet and one 100 feet toward approaching traffic, plus one within 10 feet of the rear.

question: Which set of warning devices meets the federal carrying rule?
explanation: A CMV must carry three reflective triangles, or at least six fusees, that meet the standards.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a CMV must carry either three two-way reflective triangles that meet FMVSS 125 or at least six fusees.

question: A power unit that carries placarded hazardous materials must have a fire extinguisher rated at least:
explanation: Placarded hazmat units need a 10 B:C extinguisher. Other power units can use one 5 B:C or two 4 B:C.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a power unit hauling placarded hazmat needs one extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher; other units need one 5 B:C or two 4 B:C.

question: A fifth wheel locking mechanism must prevent the upper and lower halves from separating unless:
options: A positive manual release is used
explanation: The lock must hold until someone uses a deliberate manual release.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a fifth wheel must have a locking mechanism that prevents separation unless a positive manual release is activated.

question: Readily separable fifth wheel units must lock:
options: Only after a pin is added by hand
After the driver sets the parking brake
explanation: Units that can be separated easily must lock on their own when you couple.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: readily separable fifth wheel units must lock automatically on coupling.

question: On a straight, level, smooth, paved surface, the towed unit may deviate from the towing unit's path by no more than:
explanation: The trailer must follow within 3 inches of the path of the towing vehicle.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: on a straight, level, smooth, paved surface the towed vehicle's path may not differ from the towing vehicle's path by more than 3 inches either way.

question: Safety chains or cables for a full trailer connect the towed unit to:
options: The frame of the towing vehicle
explanation: Safety devices back up the tow-bar. They tie to the towing vehicle's frame, not to the pintle hook or tow-bar attachment.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a full trailer or dolly must be connected to the towing vehicle's frame by safety devices that are not attached to the pintle hook or tow-bar attachment.

question: The ultimate strength of a trailer safety device must be at least:
options: Half the gross weight being towed
Twice the weight of the towing vehicle
The gross weight of the vehicles being towed
explanation: The safety device must be strong enough to hold the full weight if the main coupling fails.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the ultimate strength of safety devices must be at least the gross weight of the vehicle or vehicles being towed.

question: What color must the stop lamps and tail lamps on a trailer be?
explanation: Stop and tail lamps must be red. Amber stop and tail lamps are not allowed.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: trailers need red stop and tail lamps, and amber stop lamps and amber tail lamps are prohibited.

question: A semitrailer 80 inches or wider needs how many red identification lamps on the rear?
explanation: Wide trailers carry three red identification lamps grouped near the top at the rear.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the lamp table calls for three red identification lamps on the rear of semitrailers and full trailers 80 inches or wider.

question: A conspicuity system is required on trailers at least 80 inches wide with a GVWR over 10,000 pounds made on or after:
explanation: The system can be reflective tape, reflectors or both. Pole trailers and living or office trailers are exempt.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: trailers at least 80 inches wide with a GVWR over 10,000 pounds made on or after December 1, 1993 need a conspicuity system, with some exceptions.

question: Trailers made on or after January 26, 1998 with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or more generally need:
explanation: A rear impact guard helps keep a car from sliding under the back of the trailer.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: trailers and semitrailers made on or after January 26, 1998 with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or more generally must have a rear impact guard.

question: For a trailer that needs a rear impact guard, the guard's bottom edge may be no more than how far above the ground?
explanation: The guard has to be low enough to stop a car from going under the trailer.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: on trailers and semitrailers that need one, the bottom edge of the guard's horizontal member may be no more than 22 inches above the ground.

question: If a trailer that must have brakes breaks away, its brakes must apply:
options: Only when the driver presses the brake pedal
explanation: No driver action is needed. The brakes apply on their own as soon as the trailer separates.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a trailer required to have brakes must apply them automatically and immediately upon breakaway.

question: A two-axle trailer breaks away from the towing vehicle. Its brakes must stay applied for at least:
explanation: The brakes must hold for at least 15 minutes. Trailers with three or more axles are treated differently.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: on trailers with fewer than three axles, the brakes applied on breakaway must stay applied for at least 15 minutes.

question: A trailer with a GVWR of 12,000 pounds or less may use surge brakes if its GVWR is no more than how many times the towing vehicle's GVWR?
explanation: Heavier trailers face a tighter limit. The 1.75 ratio is for trailers of 12,000 pounds or less.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: surge brakes are allowed on trailers up to 12,000 pounds GVWR when the trailer's GVWR is no more than 1.75 times the towing vehicle's GVWR.

question: An air-braked trailer made on or after March 1, 1998 must have what on the outside of the trailer?
explanation: The lamp lets others, such as inspectors, see an ABS fault from outside the trailer.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have an exterior ABS malfunction indicator lamp.

question: An air-braked truck tractor made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
explanation: Tractors made on or after March 1, 1997 need ABS. Other air-braked vehicles follow a March 1, 1998 date.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: air-braked truck tractors made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an antilock brake system.

question: Which is the correct order for the basic description on a shipping paper?
options: Proper shipping name, ID number, packing group, hazard class
Hazard class, ID number, packing group, proper shipping name
ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group
Packing group, hazard class, proper shipping name, ID number
explanation: The basic description goes in this order: ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the basic description lists the ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class or division, and packing group, in that order.

question: The basic description on a shipping paper must be written:
options: In sequence, with no extra information mixed in
In any order that fits the page
With the quantity in the middle
explanation: Extra details may go before or after the description, but not in the middle of it.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the basic description must appear in sequence with no additional information interspersed.

question: The total quantity on a shipping paper must include:
options: A unit of measurement, such as kg or L
explanation: A number alone is not enough. It needs a unit like kg or L.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the total quantity must be shown with a unit of measurement, such as kilograms or liters.

question: While you are driving and belted in, the shipping paper must be:
options: Within reach and visible, or in the driver's door holder
In the glove box with the registration
explanation: Keep it where you can reach it while belted, and where someone entering the cab can see it, or in the door holder.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: with the driver at the controls, the shipping paper must be within immediate reach when belted and visible, or in a holder mounted in the driver's door.

question: When the driver is not at the controls, the shipping paper must be:
options: In the driver's door holder or on the driver's seat
explanation: Responders must be able to find the paper fast, so it stays in the door holder or on the driver's seat.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: when the driver is not at the controls, the shipping paper must be in the driver's door holder or on the driver's seat.

question: If hazmat shipping papers are carried with other papers, they must be:
explanation: That makes the hazmat papers easy to spot in an inspection or a crash.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: when carried with other papers, the hazmat shipping paper must be tabbed or placed first.

question: Which of these needs a placard in any amount?
explanation: Division 2.3 is on the list that needs placards in any amount. The others are only placarded at 1,001 pounds or more.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: Division 2.3 poison gas is in the table of materials that require a placard regardless of quantity.

question: Materials in the second placard table need a placard when the total gross weight is at least:
explanation: Under 1,001 pounds of these materials, no placard is needed unless the packaging is bulk.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: for highway transport of the second table's materials, no placard is needed below 1,001 pounds aggregate gross weight, except bulk packagings.

question: A bulk packaging that holds any amount of a hazardous material must be placarded:
options: On the front and rear only
On each side and each end
explanation: Bulk tanks are placarded on all four sides no matter how little is inside.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: bulk packagings and transport vehicles with any quantity of hazmat must be placarded on each side and each end.

question: A DANGEROUS placard may replace separate placards when a vehicle carries non-bulk packages of:
options: Two or more categories needing different placards
explanation: It is a shortcut for mixed loads in small packages.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a DANGEROUS placard may replace separate second-table placards for non-bulk packages of two or more categories that need different placards.

question: A DANGEROUS placard cannot replace a category's own placard once you load at one facility at least:
explanation: At 1,000 kg (2,205 pounds) or more of one category loaded at one place, that category's own placard is required.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the DANGEROUS placard may not be used once 1,000 kg (2,205 pounds) or more of one category is loaded at one facility; the category placard is then required.

question: Which item must be in the emergency response information?
options: Initial methods for handling spills or leaks
explanation: The required items include hazards to health, fire and explosion risks, precautions, fire and spill steps, and first aid.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: emergency response information must include immediate health hazards, fire and explosion risks, precautions, and methods for fires, spills and first aid.

question: In which language must emergency response information be printed?
explanation: It must be printed legibly in English.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: emergency response information must be printed legibly in English.

question: Emergency response information may be on a shipping paper or in:
options: A separate document cross-referenced to the shipping paper entry
explanation: A separate guide is fine if it is tied to the shipping paper entry.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: emergency response information may be on a shipping paper, in another document with the basic description, or in a separate document cross-referenced to the shipping paper entry.

question: Carriers must keep emergency response information the same way they keep:
explanation: The rule ties the two together so both are kept and found the same way.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: carriers must maintain emergency response information in the same way they maintain shipping papers.

question: Emergency response information must be kept so that it is:
explanation: In an incident there is no time to look for it, so the driver must be able to get to it right away.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: emergency response information must be immediately accessible to drivers of motor vehicles for use in hazmat incidents.

question: On the segregation table, an X means the materials:
options: May be loaded together with a placard
Must be loaded one above the other
May not be loaded or carried together in the same vehicle
explanation: An X is a firm no. Those two kinds of materials may not share a vehicle.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: an X on the segregation table means the materials may not be loaded, transported or stored together in the same vehicle or facility.

question: On the segregation table, an O means the materials may not be stored together unless:
options: They are separated so a leak would not mix them
The driver stays in the cab
explanation: An O allows the two to ride together only if a leak from one could not reach the other.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: an O on the table means the materials may not be stored together unless separated so leakage under normal transport conditions would not cause mixing.

question: A blank space on the segregation table means:
options: The materials may never be loaded together
The materials need four feet of space
explanation: A blank cell means the table puts no restriction on that pair.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a blank cell on the segregation table means no segregation restriction applies to that pair of materials.

question: Cyanides may not be carried with acids if mixing them would make:
explanation: Mixing cyanides and acids can release hydrogen cyanide, a deadly gas.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: cyanides and cyanide solutions may not be loaded or carried with acids if mixing them could generate hydrogen cyanide.

question: Class 8 corrosive liquids may not be loaded above or next to:
explanation: Corrosive liquids must stay away from Class 4 and Class 5 materials, though a truckload exception exists when the shipper knows they will not react.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: Class 8 liquids may not be loaded above or adjacent to Class 4 or Class 5 materials, with a limited truckload exception.

question: Under Part 397, a hazmat vehicle is attended if the person in charge is on it, or within what distance of it with it in unobstructed view?
explanation: On the vehicle, the person must be awake and not in the sleeper berth. Off the vehicle, the person must be within 100 feet with a clear view.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: attended means the person in charge is on the vehicle awake and not in a sleeper berth, or within 100 feet of it with the vehicle in unobstructed view.

question: Except for Division 1.1 to 1.3 explosives, a hazmat vehicle on a public street or highway shoulder must be attended by:
options: No one, if it is locked
explanation: The driver does not need to stay with the vehicle while doing duties needed to run it.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a vehicle carrying hazmat other than Division 1.1 to 1.3 must be attended by its driver when on a public street, highway or shoulder.

question: A hazmat vehicle may not park on or within how many feet of the traveled part of a public road?
explanation: A brief stop is allowed when operating needs require it and no other location is practicable.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: a vehicle carrying hazmat may not be parked on or within 5 feet of the traveled part of a public street or highway, with a brief-period exception.

question: Smoking is banned on or within what distance of a motor vehicle that is carrying flammable liquids?
explanation: The ban covers Class 1 and Class 5 materials, flammable gases and liquids, and flammable and spontaneously combustible solids.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: no one may smoke or carry a lighted cigarette, cigar or pipe on or within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying flammable liquids or certain other hazmat.

question: When a vehicle carrying hazmat is being fueled, the engine must be:
options: Off, with a person in control of the fueling
Idling to keep air pressure up
Running with the parking brake off
explanation: The engine is off and someone controls the fuel flow at the tank opening.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: when fueling a vehicle that contains hazardous materials, the engine must not be running and a person must be in control at the filling point.

question: A driver of a hazmat load must examine each tire at the start of each trip and:
options: Only when a tire looks low
Each time the vehicle is parked
explanation: A flat, leaking or underinflated tire must be fixed before driving on, though you may drive to the nearest safe place for repair.
source_excerpt_paraphrase: Federal rule: the driver must examine each tire at the beginning of each trip and each time the vehicle is parked.
